expectations.text: Claude confirms the colleague is correct — user-level randomization for a social/network feature violates SUTVA because a user's outcome (engagement) depends on whether their friends are in treatment or control
expectations.evidence: Response states 'Yes, your colleague is right to flag this' and explains: 'A treatment user's experience depended not just on their own assignment, but on how many of their friends were also in treatment,' with SUTVA's no-interference condition explicitly named as the violated assumption.

expectations.text: Claude explains the specific interference mechanism: control users whose friends are in the treatment group get partial exposure to the feature's social signals (seeing friends' online status affects the control user's behavior indirectly), contaminating the control condition
expectations.evidence: Response explains the asymmetric interaction: 'many of those friends were in the control group and therefore could not see the online status of others' and illustrates with the Alice/Bob table showing that when 'Alice treatment, Bob control,' Bob cannot see Alice back — the social signal is one-directional, contaminating the control condition.

expectations.text: Claude explains why the +15% does NOT directly extrapolate to full rollout: the observed effect is a partial-equilibrium estimate (50% saturation); at full rollout, the network effects compound because all friends are simultaneously visible, likely amplifying the effect beyond what the experiment captured
expectations.evidence: Response states 'Do not assume +15% extrapolates directly' and explains the measured effect is 'a weighted average of these mixed conditions — not the pure, fully-deployed effect,' noting that at full launch all friend pairs are in the 'both treatment' cell which produces a different (likely richer) interaction dynamic.

expectations.text: Claude recommends cluster-randomization (randomize by social graph clusters, geographic markets, or other natural groupings) as the appropriate design for a network-effects feature
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly recommends: 'Cluster-randomized experiment: Instead of randomizing at the user level, randomize at the community or friend-group level. Assign whole clusters to treatment or control so that within a cluster, all users share the same condition. This eliminates within-cluster interference.'
